title: Box Model visual playground
learningObjectives: Explain box model visual playground and apply it in a practical page layout.

understand.concept: A box model playground lets learners adjust content width, padding, border width, and margin while observing dimensions. It should distinguish content-box and border-box calculations, display computed outer dimensions, and label whether measurements include margin.
understand.whyItMatters: A reliable playground updates the visual model and numeric readouts from one state. It should explain that margin is outside the border box.
understand.analogy: A visual measuring tool is like a transparent ruler around a box: each layer is visible and measured separately.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a learning aid; actual sizing and layout follow CSS formatting rules.

explain.narrative: The starter shows four box-model layers through spacing and colour. Interactive controls and numeric measurements are the independent build task.

examples.explanation: The starter shows four box-model layers through spacing and colour. Interactive controls and numeric measurements are the independent build task.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example that demonstrates the topic's CSS behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Add labelled range controls for width, padding, border, and margin. Show content width, border-box width, and margin-inclusive occupied width. Add a content-box/border-box switch.
practise.independentTask: Build a small component that demonstrates this concept. Test it with longer content and at a narrow viewport.
hints: Change one value at a time.
Inspect computed styles in developer tools.
Check keyboard and touch access when the example has controls.

practice.starterCode: Content
practice.resetCode: Content

questions.prompt: Which four layers should a box model playground distinguish?
questions.explanation: These are the four standard layers of the CSS box model.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable way to understand a layout measurement?
options: Inspect the computed result and change one input at a time
Assume all units use the viewport as their reference
questions.answer: Inspect the computed result and change one input at a time
questions.explanation: The browser's computed result reveals how the value resolves in its actual context.
